newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stocks fall led by oil marketers.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stocks fall led by oil marketers.

text.p: Shares of petroleum marketing companies led the losers on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday on persistent dumping, dealers said.
The all-share index rose to 8420.78 from 8418.25 on Monday.
Dealers said oil shares were in trouble because of lack of investors' interest in the sector, which until recently the toast of the market in oil-producing Nigeria.
"Investors are shedding their holding in oil stocks due to their falling profitability," said one.
Oil companies blame low profit margin on sales of oil products allowed by the government for their current plight.
Unipetrol was 30 kobo down on Tuesday, closing at 67.00 naira. Agip was down 20 kobo at 16.50 naira while African Petroleum fell 10 kobo to 54.50 naira.
Two of the nations biggest banks also fell with oil shares.
Union Bank closed 30 kobo down at 8.70 naira and First Bank went down 10 kobo at 12.90 naira.
Healthcare company Smithkline Beecham ended 15 kobo lower at 5.50 naira and Union Dicon Salt dropped 20 kobo to 51.00 naira.
Cappa and D'Alberto at 12.60 naira was up 10 kobo again, following on Monday's similar appreciation.
United Bank for Africa continued to attract buyers, rising five kobo to 12.80 naira. Wema Bank also added five kobo to 3.95 naira.
Guinness, at 745 naira, and Afprint at 2.45 naira also appreciated by five kobo.
